Stated Claim / Post Context:
Urgent warning issued for Americans in the UK after attempted 'terrorist attack' as citizens are told to 'exercise caution'

The US government has issued a warning for Americans to 'exercise caution' in the UK after an attempted 'terrorist act' near an air force base.

Actual Article Body:
By LAUREN ACTON-TAYLOR, US NEWS REPORTER

Published:  05:54 AEST, 28 September 2026   |  Updated:  08:47 AEST, 28 September 2026

The US government has issued a warning for Americans to 'exercise caution' in the UK after an attempted terrorist act near an air force base.

The US Embassy in the UK said the agency had been made 'aware' of the arrests of five men in Fairford who were 'looking to do big damage' to US forces and warned citizens to remain cautious on Sunday.

'The US Embassy is aware of arrests on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act near the Royal Air Force base in Fairford, UK,' the agency said in a release.

'US citizens are encouraged to exercise caution and be mindful of personal security. US citizens are advised to follow instructions of local authorities for their personal safety and security.'

RAF Fairford, in Gloucestershire, is the US Air Force's command outpost for operations from Europe and has been used for American strikes on Iranian missile sites that have been attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The base was the subject of a warning from Iran's Revolutionary Guard in July, with the regime warning Britain not to allow US bombers to fly from the base.

President Donald Trump praised the UK police response and suggested authorities already had the suspects under investigation.

'It was fantastic. Working with Britain, it was an amazing job. We had them under investigation. They were looking to do big damage to our fort, and working with the British worked out great,' he told reporters in Illinois.

The US Embassy in the UK said the agency had been made 'aware' of the arrests of five men in Fairford who were 'looking to do big damage' to US forces and warned citizens to remain cautious on Sunday

Five men were pictured as police arrested them on terror charges this morning near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire

Heavily-armed personnel are seen at the main entrance to RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire

'It may have been Scotland Yard, I don't know. We worked with a lot of them. We had them under view for a long time, and we got them. Thank you.'

The arrests are not believed to be part of a pre-planned operation, meaning police were previously unaware of the plot.

A local farmer was said to have alerted police over the alleged car bomb plot after stumbling upon five 'Middle Eastern-looking, masked' men on the way home from a party.

'I just thought what the hell are they doing… I saw a group of Middle Eastern-looking young guys running off through the trees. Some of them had masks or balaclavas on, and they all scattered ahead of us as we drove back past.

'Some of them ran into the fields, and some of them turned to run towards the air base. We realised this was something pretty serious,' she told the Telegraph.

The heroic local farmer is understood to have raised the alarm by dialling 999 at 12.45am to report men 'acting suspiciously' around three white vans. Viable incendiary devices and chemicals were found inside one of the vehicles, police said.

She said she had spotted the vehicles 'blocking the road' before seeing a 'large group of hooded and 'balaclava'd' men' while driving home.

Around 85 homes were evacuated from the nearby Cotswolds countryside as armed police and the SAS swooped in while the Army's specialist explosive ordnance disposal team searched for more bombs.

They were reported around 12.45am by a heroic local who saw them 'acting suspiciously' near three white vans close to the perimeter of the air base, which were later found to contain viable incendiary devices

Maggie Blyth, Temporary Chief Constable for Gloucestershire Police, said the incident was now believed to have been 'contained'.
